guidelines.detail: refines FLOW-06 (The missing flows show that the alternative item-handling outcomes were not connected to the shared check, and that the check and its decision were not connected to the continuation. This makes FLOW-06’s guidance to trace branches and join paths more specific for this situation.)

same as LRN-036 (The generated start-event label is generic, while the description provides a process title and describes the initial work. This supports using labels that preserve the description’s meaning; the learned guideline LRN-036 already expresses that principle.)

refines ACT-07 (The description places the duration test after waiting for the product to arrive, and the penalty is conditional on that test. The reference’s gateways branch to the penalty and rejoin before registration; the generated boundary event uses a different BPMN structure. This refines ACT-07 by specifying how to model a decision based on the duration of a completed wait.)

same as LRN-075 (The description makes the penalty conditional on waiting more than 10 days. The generated boundary event differs from the reference decision gateway, and the reference rejoins the paths before the next common activity. This is already stated essentially the same way in LRN-075.)

same as LRN-074 (The description supports a shared completion check after either outcome of processing a member, then a decision to continue or finish. The generated model routes both outcomes through a gateway before the check and adds an unsupported selection task, while the reference flows connect the outcomes directly to the check. This is already captured in substance by LRN-074.)

refines FID-03 (The description gives a process title and no explicit start trigger, while the generated start event uses the generic label “Start.” FID-03 calls for meaningful event labels; this guideline clarifies how to label a start event when no trigger is stated.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description gives alternative outcomes for handling an individual item, followed by a check of the larger set and a decision about whether to continue processing items: Connect each alternative outcome path to the shared check. Model an explicitly described check as an activity before a condition-based gateway, and route the gateway’s outcomes to the described continuation or completion paths.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description gives alternative outcomes for handling an individual item, followed by a check of the larger set and a decision about whether to continue processing items

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes related actions, events, or outcomes that could otherwise be confused: Label each BPMN element so the stated distinctions remain clear; do not substitute a related action or use a generic label that could refer to multiple described actions or outcomes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an identifiable process trigger or activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description makes a later action conditional on whether a completed wait exceeded a stated duration: Model the condition with a decision gateway after the wait, route the conditional action on the appropriate branch, and rejoin the paths before the next common activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description makes a later action conditional on whether a completed wait exceeded a stated duration

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description provides a process title but does not state an explicit start trigger: label the start event with the process title rather than a generic label
rules_sent_back.situation: the description provides a process title but does not state an explicit start trigger
